source_evidence: By the time your order reaches the market, the price of the stock could be slightly -- or very -- different.
answer: Executing an order means getting your buy or sell instruction to a market where the trade can be completed. Your order is sent to your broker, who decides where to route it. Execution takes time, and stock prices can change while the order is in transit, so you may receive a different price from the one you saw when placing the order.
